Down the beach to Puerto Morelos town — the beach keeps going south past the resort: about 3.2 km (≈40-minute walk, or a 10-minute taxi) to the town strip and these seven spots.

Walking routes — checked Nov 2, 2026 (pins re-verified against the restaurants' own listings; order below is the real north-to-south order on the ground)

  • On foot Resort beach → Puerto Morelos town · ≈3.2 km · ≈40 min — walk the sand south to the town strip; Pelícanos (pin 44), at the far end, is ≈45 min. Not a bike route: it's soft beach sand the whole way.
  • On foot Town stroll — pins 38–44 · ≈360 m end to end · 1–5 min between stops — the beachfront pins string along Av. Rafael E. Melgar in order: 38 La Petita → 39 La Pepita → 40 El Merkadito → 41 El Pesquero → 44 Pelícanos, with 42 El Pirata on the town square and 43 Tacos.com just off it, a block inland. The dashed gold line on the town strip traces this stroll.
Walking path Verified walking route (town strip) Pools & lazy river Pool decks Gardens & lawns Ponds & water features Beach Buildings Sea, shallows to reef

Traced from the resort's official map. The grounds are drawn from the official June 2026 resort map, in that map's own tilted orientation: entrance and lobby at the top, Buildings 1–3 down the west side, the spa island and lazy river at the center, Buildings 4–5 along the bottom, Building 6 stepping diagonally, Building 7 down the oceanfront, Building 8 at the bottom-right, and the beach and sea down the right side. Building footprints, pool shapes, and spacing follow the official map's proportions — it is a stylized drawing, not a survey: lobby to beach is ≈350 m, about a 5-minute stroll, and an ≈100 m scale bar sits at the lower-left of the grounds. Buildings are drawn as flat footprints in the official map's own tan-and-brown style, pools sit on pale stone decks, and the sea bands from pale shallows out to the dashed reef line. Every pin is also in the numbered list below, in the same order. Zoom in on the restaurant row, the lobby plaza, the pools, the beach or the spa island and the drawing fills in with detail — named restaurant buildings with their terraces, loungers and swim-up bars on the pool decks, palapa rows on the sand, and the spa island's gardens; zoom back out and it clears away. October 2026 detail pass: every building footprint, pool, path, river branch and planting was re-measured against the official map and corrected where the zoomed drawing had drifted — no building sits in a pool or the river, no path runs through a building, no tree stands on a roof or on the sand, Building 7 and Building 8 stand back from the beach with the walkway and gardens between them and the sand, and the sand now runs unbroken into the wet sand and the sea with no grass strip in between. Flagged, not guessed: where the official map's own lines are ambiguous at this scale — the exact centerline of a path where it weaves between the Garibaldi Square venue blocks, and the precise tips of the lazy-river branches — the drawing follows the closest readable route on the official map rather than inventing one; the Las Olas palapa sits on the sand, stopping just short of the waterline, as it does on the official map. Moving around the map: drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, or use the + / − and reset buttons on the map — the Town strip button jumps straight to Puerto Morelos at the south end, where pins 38–44 sit on a schematic strip of the town (compressed, not to scale, past a break in the beach).

                  Anything else? Open Google Translate (English → Spanish)

                  • Room service runs 24 hours and is included — with your Excellence Club stay you get the upgraded Club menu. The resort only publishes the room service menu inside the Excellence Collection app, so browse it there; there's no public copy to put on this page.
                  • The bars pour a full premium list but publish no itemized drink menus — the Martini Bar's "tini" list, Revive's smoothies, and every other bar's list live at the bar itself. Hours are on each bar's pin.
                  • Dinner dress codes: "Casual Elegance" (Magna, Chez Isabelle, Spice) means long pants and a collared shirt — no shorts or flip-flops. "Regular Casual" allows Bermudas and a polo.
                  • Only one reservation: the teppanyaki tables at Spice. Everything else is walk-in.
                  • Book the spa hydrotherapy circuit early — Friday or Saturday of your stay — and ask about the temazcal session while you're there.
                  • Two temporary moves: Chez Isabelle's menu is currently served at Flavor Market, and Agave's at Oregano, while those rooms are refreshed. Barcelona and Toscana have closed for good.
                  • Fresh catch on the beach: the closest thing to fishermen cooking their catch near the resort is down in Puerto Morelos town (pins 38–44) — El Pesquero and Pelícanos by the pier serve the local boats' fish; ask what's fresh that day. There's no catch-of-the-day stand on the resort's own beach.

                  Beyond the town pins above, these are the names that come up again and again in traveler forums and local guides — including r/snorkeling threads and Puerto Morelos residents. The cenotes sit inland on the Ruta de los Cenotes: a taxi or tour drive of about 20–30 minutes, not a walk.

                  Rechecked Nov 2, 2026: the prices and hours below were checked again against current listings on Nov 2, 2026. Listings vary and small operators change prices without notice — treat every figure as approximate and confirm at the pier or the gate before you set out.

                  • Reef snorkeling from the town pier — r/snorkeling regulars send first-timers here instead of the hotel beach: the reef sits just offshore and small local boats at the pier run short trips. Guided pier tours now run about $35–50 a person, and some add a $10 reef park tax on top. Go early, before the wind picks up. How the advice breaks down →
                  • Cenote La Noria — the local-feel pick on the Ruta: a cavern cenote with a big opening overhead, a floating platform, and picnic tables — travelers contrast it with the big tour-bus stops. Entry is running about 400 MXN. Ruta de los Cenotes guide →
                  • Cenote Zapote — the deep one, famous among divers for the "Hells Bells" mineral formations; the park around it adds ziplines and ATV trails if swimming isn't enough. Confirmed open, 9 AM–6 PM; a swim runs about $35, or $99 for the all-inclusive tour. Cenote route overview →
                  • Cenote Siete Bocas — seven openings in the cave roof; you swim from one shaft of light to the next under the stalactites. Entry reports run 300–500 MXN. Practical note: rideshares don't map it well — arrange for your taxi to wait, or book the return ride before you go in. Cenote route overview →
                  • Cenote Verde Lucero — open-air, emerald-green, and usually the quietest of the four, at about km 17 on the same road. Entry is about 300 MXN, cash (some listings say 350). Ruta de los Cenotes guide →
                  • Cenote Las Mojarras — the big open swim on the Ruta, at km 12.6 — the closest of these cenotes: at 67 m across it's the largest open cenote in the area, with a 6 m jump platform and a zipline. A swim runs about $250 MXN; open 8 AM–5 PM. Cenote route overview →
                  • Jardín Botánico Dr. Alfredo Barrera Marín (Ya'ax Ché) — a 65-hectare jungle garden on Highway 307 at Km 320, just south of Puerto Morelos town: shaded trails, Maya ruin remains and a replica Maya home, a suspension bridge, and an observation tower over the canopy. Hours are listed Mon–Fri 8 AM–4 PM (some listings say Mon–Sat); entry reports vary, roughly 120–220 MXN, so treat that as approximate and confirm at the gate. Bring water, long pants, and bug spray. Find it on the map →
                  • Croco Cun Zoo — on Highway 307 at Km 31, just north of Puerto Morelos: an interactive guided tour of about 60–75 minutes where you can hold a baby crocodile, touch a boa, feed deer, and watch free-roaming spider monkeys. Open daily 9 AM–5 PM; about $30 for adults, $20 for children ages 6–12, and free under 5. Find it on the map →
                  • The leaning lighthouse (Faro Inclinado) and the town square — the free one: Puerto Morelos' tilted lighthouse by the town pier is the photo landmark of the town, and the square around it has artisan stalls and murals to wander. It pairs naturally with the town restaurant pins already on the map (pins 38–44) — make it the start or end of that walk. Find it on the map →

                  A personal appeal from the Spud Lord

                  Dear resort map reader, please don't scroll past this one-minute read. 98% of our readers don't give; they look the other way. If everyone using this map right now gave the price of one poolside beer, the Spud Lord's tab would be covered for the entire trip.

                  This map was built with love and an unreasonable number of late nights — every pin checked, every menu typed in — so nobody in this crew has to wander the resort lost. It will always be free. The beer, regrettably, is not.

                  Spud Arcade

                  Nine games, one spud.

                  New · 3D

                  Tate-lo 3D — Spudball FPS

                  First person, maxed out: four arenas, five sour-cream blasters, five modes, and power-ups on the field — WASD and mouse or twin sticks, one hit and you're a splat.

                  Tate-lo — Spudball

                  Top-down, maxed out: four arenas, five sour-cream blasters, five modes, and power-ups on the field — twin drag-sticks and the SPLAT button, one hit and you're a splat. Drop-in multiplayer: press A and you're in the live room with whoever's playing — bots fill the empty slots and step aside as people arrive. Join mid-round and you spectate until the next round.

                  🏎️ Spud Kart — Resort Grand Prix

                  Three tracks now: the sunset Resort Grand Prix, the guardrail-free Prism Spud Skyway in the sky, and the twisty Twilight Mash Mile. Drop-in multiplayer: press A and you're in the live room — bots fill the empty grid slots and step aside as people arrive, and everyone races with the same items. Topping boxes hand out the whole fork family (straight, homing, and the leader-hunting Golden Leader Fork), Superstar Spud invincibility, Thunder Mash shrink lightning, Rocket Russet autopilot bursts, boosts, shields and butter traps. Hit the ramps, trick mid-air for a boost, and grab Spud Coins to nudge your top speed up.

                  SuperSpud Runner — Maxed Out

                  The original, loaded: SuperSpud runs through four worlds — Sunset Rooftops, Starlight Spud City, Buttercup Meadow, and the Sour Cream Snowcaps. Dodge forks, knives, mashers, butter slicks, hover peelers, and runaway rolling pins; collect seven toppings; and grab the Spud Magnet, Sour Cream Shield, and Double-Loaded ×2 power-ups. Distance milestones pay bonus points as the run gets faster and meaner.

                  New · Cards · Multiplayer

                  Peel Out! — Maxed Out

                  The potato shedding game, loaded: match color or number and ditch your whole hand first. New cards — Tater Trade, The Grater, the Mash-Up Wheel — join Skips, Flips, Double Fries, the Wild Spud and Fully Loaded +4. The table picks its own rules: stacking fries, jump-in plays, 7/0 hand swaps and rotations, draw-till-it-plays. Bots come in three levels, and tournament mode crowns a champion across games. Drop in anytime — you deal into the next game.

                  New · Cards · Multiplayer

                  Fuck the Dealer — Maxed Out

                  Guess the next card. Wrong? The dealer only says higher or lower — guess again. Blow it twice and you drink; nail it and the dealer drinks. Now loaded: four modes (Classic, Speed Smash against the clock, Team Mash, Double Mash), three ways the deck rotates, 2–5 strikes to pass it, single or double decks, three table difficulties, and four bot guessers with styles of their own — the Card Counter, the Hot-Streak Chaser, the Chaotic Sprout, and the Pattern Peeler. Streaks, dealer stands, and a running leaderboard included. Join the circle anytime.

                  New · Strategy · RTS

                  SpudCraft — Potato RTS

                  A full real-time strategy war over the garden: pick one of three potato factions — the balanced Yukon Gold Union, the tank-tough Russet Combine, or the lightning-fast Purple Majesty Court — then harvest starch and butter, raise a Root Cellar warren, train Sproutlings, Peel Pikemen, Russet Rushers, Mash Maulers and Cream Casters, research upgrades at the Butter Works, and fight through fog of war. Three maps, three bot difficulties, skirmish mode, and a three-mission campaign: First Harvest, Hold the Mash, and The Full Feast.

                  New · Farming Sim

                  SpudValley — Potato Farming

                  A whole farming life in one valley: plant potatoes and eleven other crops across four seasons, ride the day from 6 AM to midnight, ship your harvest for gold, upgrade your tools, house, and farm, raise chickens and cows, fish the pond, delve a mine full of Starch Slimes, befriend the seven folk of Tuber Town with gifts and chat, cook in your farmhouse kitchen, and join a festival every season. Three farm slots save right on this device.

                  New · Monster Adventure

                  SpudMonsters — Potato Monster Adventure

                  Catch 'em, mash 'em, love 'em: wander Tuber Town and four wild grounds, meet wild potato monsters in the tall grass, and catch them with Spud Balls in turn-based battles. A 39-entry SpudDex of original spuds across seven types — with level-up evolutions, a Daycare that breeds eggs, and a Fusion Lab where two monsters combine into a brand-new one. Earn Spud Coins, stock up at the shop, beat four gyms for their badges, then climb the Full Plate league to face the Grand Mashter. Three trainer slots save right on this device.

                      Resort Grand Prix

                      Three laps of the sunset coast road — palms, sea air, and butter on the asphalt.

                      Three laps, three rival spuds, one golden kart. Your kart rolls on its own — steer with ◀ ▶, the arrow keys, or A / D, brake with ▼ or S for tight corners. Dragging on the road steers too.

                      Hit a ? topping box, then press Space or the Item button: Turbo Tater boost, Sour Cream Shield, Butter Trap, the Tater Fork (straight shot), the Seeking Spud Fork (it homes in), the Golden Leader Fork (it hunts whoever's first), Superstar Spud invincibility, Thunder Mash lightning that shrinks every rival, and the Rocket Russet autopilot burst. Trailing racers draw the stronger stuff — and bots and live rivals race with the exact same items.

                      Orange ramps launch you — tap Space or the Item button mid-air to trick and land with a boost. Gold Spud Coins on the road each nudge your top speed up a little (up to +12%). Butter slicks spin you out unless you're shielded, starred, or rocketing. And on the Prism Spud Skyway there's no guardrail: slide off the edge and you drop — then get fished back onto the road, a few seconds poorer.

                      Live room: press A (or tap Join) and you're in with whoever's racing right now — no lobby, no invites, no name form. Bots fill the empty grid slots and step aside as people arrive, and a bot takes your slot if you leave. Join mid-race and you spectate until the next race.

                      Skip (Mash) jumps the next spud · Flip reverses the order (with two players it acts as a Skip) · +2 Double Fry makes the next spud draw two and lose their turn · Wild Spud plays on anything · Fully Loaded is a wild +4 · Tater Trade swaps your hand with the next spud's · The Grater makes every other spud draw 1 · the Mash-Up Wheel is a wild that rotates every hand one seat.                           Modes: Classic Circle is the original game · Speed Smash puts every guess on a clock (25s on the Sprout Table, 15s at Home, 10s for Masters; the second guess gets 60% of that) and a freeze costs a sip · Team Mash seats the circle Gold Spuds vs Red Spudtans, alternating chairs, and the dealer's team sips when a guess lands · Double Mash pays 3 sips for a first-try hit, 2 for a second-guess hit, and costs 2 for a double miss. Deck passes: Circle Pass moves the deck one seat, Steal the Deck hands it to the guesser who finished the strikes, and King Spud keeps the deck and drinks a bonus instead. Streaks count your hits in a row; a dealer's “stand” counts guessers turned away in a row. Sips are tracked on the honor system — the app counts them, your cup is your business. Joining mid-game drops you straight into the circle; you guess when the turn reaches you.

                          Economy: Sproutlings dig starch patches (+10 a trip) and skim butter springs (+6 a trip) — butter pays for heavy units and every Butter Works upgrade. Buildings: Root Cellar (HQ — trains Sproutlings, takes deliveries), Skillet Barracks (trains the army), Butter Works (Sharp Peels, Thick Skins, Swift Sprouts research), Sour Cream Tower (defense turret), Cold Storage (+8 supply, extra drop-off). Fog of war: black is unscouted, dim is remembered ground, bright is what your spuds can see right now. Destroy the enemy Root Cellar to win — lose yours and the war is over.

                          Your party & the Root Cellar Box

                          Root Cellar Box

                          Your lead spud fights first. Eggs ride along and hatch after won battles — they can't fight. Mash Tonics heal 60 HP, in or out of battle.

                          SpudDex — collection log

                          The Spud Shop

                          Golden Balls catch at 1.5× and Loaded Balls at 2.2× the standard Spud Ball. The Mash Center next door heals your whole party and restores every move, free, forever.

                          The Daycare — breeding

                          Leave any two of your spuds together and the Daycare finds an egg: 100 coins. The egg hatches after 3 won battles into a Lv 1 baby of the first parent's base form, carrying one of the second parent's moves.

                          The Fusion Lab

                          Two monsters go into the Mash Chamber — one brand-new monster comes out. The result is set by the pair's main types, it's a touch stronger than either parent, and it keeps two moves from each. The parents are gone for good. 200 coins a fusion.

                          Gyms of Tuber Town

                          The Full Plate League

                          Explore with WASD or the arrow keys, the touch pad, or tap-to-walk. Interact with E. In battle, tap a move (or press 1–4), C throws a Spud Ball, T uses a Mash Tonic, R runs from a wild fight. Gyms must fall in order; the League Hall opens once you hold all four badges. Wild levels climb from Sprout Meadows to Spice Ridge — train, evolve, breed, and fuse a team worthy of the Grand Mashter.
